description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 6b439ac5947fccc105ec83faf60568d15e24d2a9 -->

## What's Changed
### Features
* Analyse references to properties by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13955
### Fixes
* Fix explode() return type with a negative limit by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13949
* Report native return types disjoint from the inherited @return docblock by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13951
* Narrow strings by strlen() comparisons that imply non-emptiness one way by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13953
* Drop null from the left side of ?? on ArrayAccess offsets (#9960) by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12738
* Don't assume an implicit null return after exhaustive type checks by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13952
* Cast numeric-string and float array keys to int by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13956
* Take an offset bound by reference as created, and its null array as an array by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13954
* Narrow loop counters with the exit condition and inc/dec conditions by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13950
* Do not make a key optional when the unsealed arrays lacking it may hold it by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13904
* Narrow the receiver of a nullsafe chain that is not identical to null by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12701
* Fix superglobal made nullable by global by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13973
* Fix UndefinedVariable in isset() after a switch whose later case ends in a conditional throw by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13974
* Fix: RedundantCondition on a nullsafe fetch compared to a bool literal by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13945
* Fix crash destructuring an ArrayAccess object of self by @shu-chen-dot-ca in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13785
* Fix: nullsafe fetch on an unread non-null property receiver is typed nullable by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13946
* Resolve static in template arguments when comparing inherited signatures by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14000
* Fix: PHP 8.6 SodiumCryptoXof*State classes are undefined by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14013
* Handle break 2 out of a nested switch by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13991
* Fix UnusedVariable for an assignment before a break or in a catch read after the enclosing if by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13981
* Narrow the value a loop exits with through ++/-- in its condition by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13992
* Fix UndefinedVariable for a variable assigned in a nested && operand by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13976
* Fix: properties of builtin classes known only through reflection are mixed by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14015
* Keep the memoized result of a call that may change it by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13990
* Fix: `curl_multi_get_handles()` returns `array<array-key, mixed>` instead of `list<CurlHandle>` by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14022
* Fix: PHP 8.6 global constants are undefined when Psalm runs on PHP < 8.6 by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14024
* Fix: a parent's @method overriding a non-public method of the child where the call reaches it by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14016
* Replace characters XML 1.0 forbids in checkstyle and JUnit reports by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14025
* Fix: PHP 8.6 signatures of `socket_addrinfo_lookup()`, `socket_cmsg_space()` and `ldap_free_result()` by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14023
* Inherit Iterator methods on interfaces extending RecursiveIterator and other internal interfaces by @orklah in https://github.com/vim

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
